title: Coherence graph edge
description: A constraint between surfaces that must hold simultaneously. Most real detections are a broken edge rather than a wrong value, so edges are first-class rows with their own owner.

members.description: Surface ledger ids bound by this constraint.

constraint.description: The relation in plain language, e.g. 'navigator.platform, UA OS token and Client Hints platform must name the same OS'.

check.description: A human-readable statement of the invariant, written in expression form. NOTHING EVALUATES IT. No script in this repository reads this field: ledger/coherence.jsonl is consumed only by scripts/validate-ledger.py and scripts/merge-inbox.py, neither of which looks at `check`, and capture/derive/conform.py is a probe-by-probe diff with no expression evaluator. The field this row's gate is named in is `enforced_by`. This description previously called `check` an 'executable predicate over a collected fingerprint, used by the V3 conformance runner', and that sentence is why nine invented field names went unchallenged: an expression nobody runs has nothing to reject it. A statement that names a field no profile carries is still wrong as prose, so the vocabulary is closed. Exactly four namespaces are allowed. (1) `profile.<path>`: a key path declared in config/profile.schema.json, spelled as scripts/check-schema-wiring.py spells a declared path - dotted, `[]` for an array item, `*` for an additionalProperties child - so this file and the `profile_field` column of ledger/surfaces.jsonl share one vocabulary. (2) `host.<path>`: the launch host's real pre-spoof value of that same declared path, e.g. host.cpu.logical_cores. (3) `fp['<probe id>']`: the collected fingerprint, meaning probes['<probe id>'].value of a capture/schema/capture.schema.json document, where <probe id> is one capture/collector/collector.js actually registers; single-quoted subscript only, and anything after the subscript is the probe's own JSON. (4) Everything else: operators, literals, page-level JavaScript read the way a page would read it, named helper predicates, and corpus lookups such as corpus_row_for(...) whose argument must itself come from (1) to (3). A value's source MUST carry one of the three prefixes; a bare identifier is a helper parameter, never a data reference. Three spellings are banned because each was a live defect: `profile['<surface id>']`, indexing the profile by surface ledger id; `profile.<dispersion axis>`, because an axis is a composition selector and resources/profiles/dispersion/machine_class.json states that it emits no profile field; and `fp['<unregistered probe>']`.

enforced_by.description: Every gate that actually makes this invariant hold, and nothing else. An EMPTY ARRAY means nothing enforces the edge; that is a legitimate and common value, it is counted and printed by scripts/check-schema-wiring.py on every run, and it is never a failure. The field is required so that a row cannot drop out of that count by omission. Assignment rules, so the array is not an opinion: `resolver` where composition cannot emit a profile that violates the invariant; `patch` where either every member surface is served by one single profile field that a sequenced patch reads, so the members have one source and cannot disagree, or the patch directly implements the invariant; `v3-probe` where every observable the statement names is recorded in that probe AND none of them is excluded by conform.py's ALWAYS_VOLATILE or VOLATILE_PATHS, so a V3 diff against the reference device decides the edge.

site.description: resolver: 'scripts/profile_resolver.py:<function>', which must exist, be called in that file, and carry a '# coh: <this row's id>' marker comment on the condition that enforces this edge - the marker is what keeps the claim falsifiable when the condition is deleted. patch: an entry exactly as it appears in patches/series, which must also exist on disk. v3-probe: 'capture/collector/collector.js:<probe id>', a probe id the collector registers.

unbuilt_dependency.description: Things this invariant needs that the fork has not built. Present only where the statement is RIGHT about something missing, never where it names the wrong thing - that is a defect to fix, not to annotate, and merging the two would lose the difference between 'this row is wrong' and 'this row is right about something we have not built'. Carried on the row rather than in an allowlist inside a checker, and falsifiable in both directions the way profile_field_exception is, so an annotation that outlives its problem fails too.

key.description: A profile key path in declared-path spelling, e.g. network.local_interfaces.

reason.description: undeclared: config/profile.schema.json declares no such key, so no profile can carry the value and the surface stays inherited from the host. The key MUST NOT resolve; one that has since been declared is a stale annotation. unconditioned: the key is declared and consumed, but no dispersion axis varies it, so one value is served under every seed and every claimed platform - which is both a cross-seed linking property and an unchecked platform claim. The key MUST resolve, and no dispersion table may offer two or more distinct values for it; the moment an axis varies it, the annotation is stale.

severity.description: fatal: a violation is decisive on its own. strong: decisive when corroborated. weak: never sufficient alone. Mirrors the ruling algebra so weak signals cannot accumulate into false certainty.

status.description: May only become 'resolved' on T0 or T1 evidence. T2 and T3 can open a row, never close one. See docs/METHODOLOGY.md §3.
